data.summary: Extracts the content of the <reversed_text>...</reversed_text> tag from the final assistant message, using the same non-greedy, whitespace-stripping pattern as the original parser. The first tag (the one the original grader scores) or the last tag is accepted. The extracted text is Unicode NFC-normalized and stripped, then must equal the stripped, normalized gold exactly: case-sensitive, with punctuation and inner spaces preserved. A response that passes keeps its original reward unchanged. Anything else, including case flips, truncations, partially unreversed words or a missing tag, gets 0.0. This closes the fuzzy SequenceMatcher-ratio loophole.

The grader reads the first <reversed_text>...</reversed_text> block in the final assistant message, the same block the original parser scores, and strips surrounding whitespace. It keeps the original reward only when that content exactly equals the stripped gold answer. The match is case-sensitive and keeps punctuation and inner spacing; the only normalization is Unicode NFC, so canonically equivalent characters still match. A missing tag, or any mismatch (case flips, truncation, partly unreversed words), scores 0.0. Regex patterns are passed directly to re.search, with no compile() call.

Extracts every <reversed_text>...</reversed_text> block in the final assistant message (not just the first). The reward is set to 0 when no block exists, when an opening tag has no matching close, or when any block (after NFC normalization and whitespace stripping) differs from the gold. Otherwise the original reward is returned unchanged. Each block must equal the gold exactly, case and punctuation included. This keeps the earlier fixes for fuzzy SequenceMatcher partial credit. It also closes the multi-answer loophole, where a correct first tag hid a different final answer.
